headline: Mistakes to Avoid When Cleaning Up Kitchen Fire Damage
articleBody: A kitchen fire can be super stressful, and it's natural to want to jump in and clean things up right away. But hold on a second! There are some common mistakes folks make that can actually cause more damage or even put their health at risk. First, don't try to clean up soot and ash without proper protection. Those tiny particles are really corrosive and can spread easily, making the problem worse if you don't have the right equipment. Next, never use household cleaners on fire-damaged surfaces. They might react poorly with soot, setting stains permanently or just making a bigger mess. Also, opening windows and doors indiscriminately can seem like a good idea for ventilation, but it can sometimes make soot spread further due into other unaffected areas of your home due to air currents. It's better to consult with professionals who understand how to contain the damage. Don't forget about hidden moisture, too – extinguishing efforts can leave behind water that leads to mold if not dried properly. Finally, putting off professional cleanup can be a huge misstep. The longer fire and smoke damage sits, the harder and more costly it becomes to restore.
